data_findings:
All figures below were re-checked against the samples this session (pure-Python DuckDB queries and a compiled integration test).
- Time Behind Next is a signed offset to the car one place ahead; negative means that car is ahead. Across the Race sample's 18 closed racing laps, the change in gap regresses on lap duration at -1.44 s/s, r = -0.68. Recomputed this session: slope -1.44, r -0.68, n = 18.
- Race: 2,682 readings at 2 Hz, range -8.36..+0.11, no exact zeros, and 10 sign flips. Median step 0.014 s, p99 0.113 s.
- The first 86 readings (42.5 s) are all -0.1879 (on the grid). The last 22 (10.5 s) are all -6.9584 (frozen after the flag).
- Exactly three steps of 0.4 s or more: 122.5 s (+0.113 to -0.458), 124.0 s (-0.059 to -0.712) and 165.0 s (-0.023 to -2.098). Each follows the gap closing to within 0.11 s, which is a pass. Largest ordinary step is 0.293 s and smallest change is 0.572 s, so the 0.4 s threshold sits between them.
- Lap boundaries cause no jumps.
- Qualify (Spa, 1,178 readings): range -22.26..+1.71, 61 steps of 0.3 s or more, 41 sign flips, 8.1% positive, 43 exact zeros, largest step 23.97 s.
- Practice (Interlagos, 655 readings): range -41.88..+43.40, 68 steps of 0.3 s or more, 72.5% of readings beyond ±10 s, 18 exact zeros, largest step 80.64 s. Hence the view is race-only.
- Net for the Race sample: end minus start is -6.77 s raw, of which the three passes are -3.30 s, leaving -3.47 s lost over 19 laps. Lap 1 reads +0.97 s once passes are removed (raw -2.33 s).
- Bug caught by the golden: ValueRange.ticks emits 2.5 steps, and a magnitude-only decimals rule printed -2.5, -7.5 as "-3", "-8". Fixed in formatGapTick and PerLapBarChart._tick.
spec_notes:
§8.9 "Built in v0.11": Race Pace & Gaps reads `Time Behind Next` (2 Hz, unit s) through three reads the repository already does. A session-scoped min/max-bucketed trace (1,000 buckets, used for drawing only) is fetched via readTrace with a session TraceWindow. The full-resolution series is fetched via readFullResolution, so a single 0.5 s car-ahead change is never hidden inside a bucket. Per-lap first/last/min/max/mean comes from readLapStats, and pit visits from `In Pits`. Everything derived from those is pure functions (`carAheadChangesIn`, `heldReadingsAtStart/End`, `lapGapsFrom`, `GapSession`) that a plain `flutter test` reaches. The view is race-only. Practice and Qualify return before the channel is read and show a stated explanation. Layout: five StatTiles (gap at start, gap at end, net against the car ahead, closest approach, car-ahead changes). Then a custom-painted session chart with the envelope band and line, a fill toward zero in one hue, lap strip, dimmed held stretches, rings on car-ahead changes, pit shading, a cursor with floating readout, and arrow/Home/End/Esc keys. Then a signed `PerLapBarChart` (new optional `signed` flag), the car-ahead change list, and a per-lap table carrying every charted value. A lap's gained/lost is the movement of the gap over the lap less the car-ahead-change steps, so the three passes of lap 1 read as +0.97 s gained and not -2.33 s lost. Laps with pit-lane time, no data, an exact-zero boundary, or an unfinished end are drawn grey and left out of the net.

§14 roadmap entry, findings from building it: (1) `Time Behind Next` is a signed time offset to the car one place ahead (negative = that car is ahead). Across the Race sample's 18 closed racing laps, the change in gap regresses on lap duration at -1.44 s/s (r = -0.68), which fixes the sign and says the car is the one ahead. (2) It is a timing-line gap, not distance over speed: median step 0.014 s, p99 0.113 s, and no step larger than 0.067 s within a second of any `Lap` event. (3) It is held, not zeroed, when nothing is timed: the first 86 readings (42.5 s, on the grid) are all -0.1879, and the last 22 (10.5 s, after `Finish Status` = 1) are all -6.9584. (4) A step of 0.4 s or more is a change of car ahead. The Race sample has exactly three, at 122.5 s, 124.0 s and 165.0 s, each after the gap closed to within 0.11 s. The largest ordinary step is 0.293 s and the smallest change 0.572 s. (5) Outside a race the channel is not a gap you can watch. Qualify has 61 steps of 0.3 s or more, 41 sign flips and a 23.97 s step; Practice has 68 such steps, 72.5% of readings beyond ±10 s and an 80.64 s step. The explanation that the game ranks by best lap is an inference and is worded as one. Exact zeros occur only in those two files (43 and 18) and are treated as "no car timed". (6) Not established: pit-lane behaviour (no race sample enters the pits) and what a race leader reads. (7) Net for the Race sample is -3.47 s over 19 laps; -6.96 s at the end against -0.19 s at the start is -6.77 s raw, of which -3.30 s is the three passes. (8) `ValueRange.ticks` produces 2.5 × 10ⁿ steps; any axis formatter that picks decimals from the step's size alone mislabels them (-7.5 as "-8"). The formatter now derives decimals from the step, in `formatGapTick` and `PerLapBarChart`. (9) DuckDB returns FLOAT readings widened to double (-0.18789291381835938), while the fixtures hold the shortest round-trip decimal (-0.18789291). Comparisons across the two must narrow to float32 first.
